close_reason: Seven line-number citations converted to stable section+paragraph form across task.rs (4 sites), backend.rs (2), lib.rs (1). cargo doc -D warnings + clippy + test green.
description:
crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:142-143:

    /// Compute \`utcStart\` and \`utcDue\` for a [\`Task\`](jmap_tasks_types::Task) by converting the task's
    /// \`start\`/\`due\` local-time fields and time zone into UTC (draft-tasks-06 §4,
    /// lines 739-772).

The reference to \"lines 739-772\" pins the docstring to a specific draft revision of draft-ietf-jmap-tasks. When draft-07 ships and the section is re-paginated (every IETF revision causes line drift — section anchors do not), this docstring becomes a dangling reference.

Same pattern appears in:

  - lib.rs:734 (test comment)
  - lib.rs:759 (test comment)
  - task.rs:24 (handler doc)
  - task.rs:683 (test doc)
  - task.rs:711 (test doc)
  - backend.rs:108 (\`lines 978-981\` for per-user routing)

Engineering basis: IETF drafts re-paginate on every revision. RFCs do not. Section numbers (§4.5.1, §3.5, etc.) are stable across both. Line numbers are stable only within a single revision. The crate already cites sections elsewhere (e.g. \"draft-tasks-06 §3.7\" in task_list.rs:46) — the citation style is mixed.

Fix: every \"lines X-Y\" reference becomes \"§N.M\" with the same content. Where the doc wants to point at a single paragraph within a section, the citation is \"§N.M paragraph 'utcStart MUST be computed from …'\" or similar.

This finding is labelled `opinion` because it is rote-style — the contract surface is unchanged, only the doc reference quality. Filing because the supplement template asks for api-contract,docs and the pattern is consistent enough to be worth flagging in one pass.
title: compute_task_utc_times docstring references draft line numbers ("lines 739-772") instead of section numbers — line numbers drift on every draft revision
